title: Homo floresiensis
summary: Homo floresiensis is a small-bodied hominin known only from Liang Bua cave on the Indonesian island of Flores, first found in 2003. The partial skeleton LB1 stood about 106 cm. Its fossils date to about 100,000 to 60,000 years ago, with stone tools to about 50,000. Its ancestry, whether dwarfed Homo erectus or an earlier lineage, is debated.

uncertainty.note: Years are 1950 minus the age. The Smithsonian header gives about 100,000-50,000 years ago; the fossils themselves are about 100,000-60,000 years old, and the later end rests on stone tools.

as_recorded.value: stone tools suggest survival until about 50,000 years ago

where.modern_name: Liang Bua cave, Flores, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
where.historical_name: Liang Bua, island of Flores; no states or place names exist at this date

importance.justification: A late-surviving, small-bodied hominin that changed ideas about human diversity and island evolution.
